output.claimText: The KAZ_S_159 operator completed mitigation of the 2026-06-05 detected methane plume, and a post-action measurement confirms the outcome by 2026-07-31.
output.verdict: ABSTAIN — insufficient evidence to verify the stated mitigation and post-action outcome. The claim is not established by the inspected evidence; this does not establish that no action occurred or that the claim is false.
limitations: The inspected record is a historical UNEP IMEO MARS snapshot, not a live or continuous measurement. The archive runs through 2026-09-13 UTC.

For the selected observation 7529d451-018f-4da3-9114-59b76c3a3bcd, MARS reports 307 kg/h with ± 66 kg/h standard deviation at 2026-06-05T07:40:02Z. A later in-scope overpass, 941806b5-2afe-46ac-baac-a0230880cede, reports 496 kg/h with ± 226 kg/h standard deviation at 2026-07-11T08:12:14Z. These are discrete overpasses; no action date or linkage establishes that the later record is post-action or verifies an outcome.

The 2024-06-07T08:05:04Z observation is outside the requested scope. The three records are separate overpasses; gaps or missing detections do not mean zero emissions. The publisher-supplied plume outline is not raw satellite pixels, continuous concentration, an operator response, or proof of mitigation.

The inspected UI identifies EnMAP - DLR and product IDs, but does not provide instrument footprint/valid coverage, observation opportunities, detection limits, or coverage/quality masks for interpreting a non-detection. Satellite context is shown as unavailable.
Publisher notification/response metadata is Yes (the DEMO project note says notified: Yes and feedback: Yes); these fields do not prove notice delivery, a mitigation action, or equipment repair.

One linked publisher report is listed, but its contents are not included or independently reviewed. External report metadata is withheld and was not cleared for provider processing; no excerpt was used.

The deterministic application baseline reports insufficient reference coverage. Its reference metadata analysis does not authenticate document contents or establish physical outcomes; no human assessment was recorded.

requestedEvidence.request: Provide an inspectable operator work order, maintenance log, or equivalent action record tied to KAZ_S_159 and the relevant facility/source or equipment. Identify the action, responsible party/role, and exact action/completion date and time in UTC, with a stable record ID or reference and issuer.

Provide the dated follow-up measurement for the same source/equipment, with the exact UTC timestamp, observation/product ID, measurement method and instrument, source linkage, reported flux and units, and reported uncertainty (including whether the value is a standard deviation). State the outcome criterion used to say that mitigation succeeded; do not assume zero emissions.

For the follow-up measurement, provide the applicable spatial footprint/valid coverage over the source, observation opportunities and gaps, detection limit/sensitivity, retrieval or quality flags, and the source data/document reference. Identify the issuer and date, provide exact citations, and confirm rights to inspect/process the submitted material. If action and follow-up share a calendar day, include timestamps precise enough to establish their order.

output.whyNeeded: The supplied MARS records establish dated source-linked flux estimates, but no scoped action record, action date, measurement method, or attributable post-action reference is included. The 2026-07-11 overpass follows the 2026-06-05 observation in calendar time, but without an action timestamp it cannot be identified as post-action. Instrument coverage and measurement uncertainty are needed to interpret a follow-up or any missing detection; publisher flags and a linked-report pointer do not establish the physical outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: The action record identifies the source/facility or equipment and links it to KAZ_S_159 and the relevant event; it states the action, responsible party/role, and exact UTC action/completion date and time within 2026-06-01 through 2026-07-31.
The action record has an inspectable, attributable reference with issuer, record/document ID, date, and a stable source or authorized copy.

The follow-up measurement is attributable to the same source/equipment, has an exact UTC timestamp on or after the action and within the stated scope, and cites its observation/product ID. Same-calendar-day evidence gives sufficient time precision to establish order.

The follow-up states measurement method and instrument, flux value and units, uncertainty with its type (including standard deviation if reported), and the outcome criterion used; no unprovided threshold or zero-emissions assumption is introduced.

The measurement package states relevant instrument coverage/footprint over the source, observation opportunities or gaps, detection limit/sensitivity, and applicable retrieval/quality information so that a missing detection is not treated as zero.
Issuer, exact citations, source linkage, and document/data processing rights are inspectable; any publisher report excerpt is supplied only with appropriate permission.
output.ownerRole: KAZ_S_159 source operator's maintenance/methane-mitigation records custodian for the action record; the follow-up measurement provider or instrument-data custodian for the measurement, coverage, and provenance package.

dueDateOrReasonUnset.reasonUnset: No request deadline or responsible individual is supplied. 2026-07-31 is the claim scope end date, not a source-provided evidence-request due date.

steps: Read the MethaneResponse audit page and inspected the KAZ_S_159 claim and available evidence requirements.
Inspected all three MARS observations, including the assigned 2026-06-05 record, and recorded timestamps, flux, standard deviation, instrument and product IDs.
Applied the inclusive UTC period 2026-06-01 through 2026-07-31 and ran the rules baseline.
Ran deterministic reference coverage and the bounded archive cross-check; retained their stated limits and did not treat them as physical verification.
Did not open or process the withheld publisher report and did not save a human determination.
errors: Browser select for 'Observation event' timed out; selecting 'Statement to check' also timed out. The assigned observation ID remains preserved in the submitted scope and references.
The 'Use selected observation day' action failed while preparing the wider date scope. The period-only scope was then applied successfully.

notes: Abstained from confirming physical mitigation because the supplied evidence is insufficient. A precise next-evidence request and the task log are included in output; no human help was requested.
